Additive genetic covariance

Source: R/accessors.R
additive_covariance.Rd

Least-squares additive genetic (co)variance of the current population: the covariance matrix of the best linear prediction of genotypic values from the state of every locus (the sum of its two alleles: their effect vectors, or for binary_b() their effects B y, or for contribution_matrix() the gene values). For the architectures in evomod2 the genotypic value is linear in the state of each locus given the others, so this is the additive variance in the usual sense (variance of breeding values) under linkage equilibrium. G - additive is the non-additive (epistatic) covariance. Needs more individuals than loci times traits.

Usage

additive_covariance(pop)

Arguments

pop

an evomod_population.

Value

A list with G, additive and nonadditive (G - additive), all with the n - 1 denominator of stats::cov().

Examples

eps <- pairwise_epsilon(loci = 10, traits = 2, sd = 1)
m <- evomod_model(multilinear(10, 2, eps), mutation(0.01, 0.2), env_sd = 1, init_sd = 0.1)
pop <- evolve(m, stabilizing(200, omega = 20), n = 300, seed = 1)
additive_covariance(pop)
#> $G
#>           trait1    trait2
#> trait1 1.8910878 0.1247169
#> trait2 0.1247169 1.6747977
#> 
#> $additive
#>           trait1    trait2
#> trait1 0.9021293 0.1499882
#> trait2 0.1499882 0.8469063
#> 
#> $nonadditive
#>             trait1      trait2
#> trait1  0.98895850 -0.02527132
#> trait2 -0.02527132  0.82789140
#>
